subject: Incubator credits grandfathering and ramp plan
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha@nestincubator.org>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Incubator credits question: grandfathering from last cohort

Hi Priyom,

Hope you had a great summit — quick one from our side. Our most recent cohort used Redwood during a private pilot (Q2 2027). We signed the pilot SOW under Nest’s program terms and were given a batch of promotional credits that expired at the end of the pilot. Several companies in the cohort have asked whether those unused credits can be grandfathered into the new incubator package so they can ramp pilot work into paid trials.

Practically: is Redwood open to either (A) rolling 50% of unused credits forward to our new cohort seats, or (B) issuing a one-time promotional top-up to cover onboarding months? The ask is to avoid re-doing procurement for each early-stage company.

I can share the cohort SOW and a usage CSV if that helps. We’re finalizing the incubator sponsorship package the week of Sep 27 and need to give partners clarity.

Thanks —
Sam
Samantha Li
Director, Programs | Nest Incubator
[Attachment: Nest_Incubator_SOW.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@nestincubator.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incubator credits question: grandfathering from last cohort

Hi Sam — great to hear from you and congrats on the new cohort.

Short answer: we’re open to finding a pragmatic approach so the startups can get continuity without repeating procurement. I don’t want to overpromise on an enterprise-wide policy without a quick review, but two practical paths look viable:

- Option 1: Roll-forward 50% of verified unused promo credits to the new incubator seats (applies only to accounts that were part of the original pilot).
- Option 2: One-time top-up (equivalent token value) to cover onboarding + first-node experiments for new cohort companies.

What I need from you to get internal approval: the cohort SOW (you already attached — thanks), a per-company usage CSV (we need to verify unused balance per account), and a short list of 10 companies you expect to enroll so we can estimate exposure.

I’ve looped in Ben (field sales) to confirm commercial approach; if finance/legal sign off is needed we’ll route a formal exception. I can put together a short memo and proposed amendment to the incubator offer.

Can we aim to finalize terms before Sep 30 so you can include language in the sponsor pack? If yes, please send the CSV and the expected cohort list.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Startups | Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: usage_history_sept2027.csv]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 12:12:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Incubator credits question: grandfathering from last cohort

Marissa / Naomi / Ben — forwarding Nest’s request. TL;DR: Nest is asking whether we can (a) roll 50% of unused pilot promo credits forward for cohort participants, or (b) issue a one-time top-up equivalent to onboarding months.

Quick context: this is a program-level exception for an incubator partner (very visible, recurring cohorts). Estimated footprint if we accept roll-forward across 10 companies is ~ $6k in credited token value (conservative). I’ve attached the SOW and the usage CSV they shared.

Questions for you:
- Naomi: is finance comfortable with a one-time write-off or promo credit for exposure at this magnitude? If so, do we need a specific accounting code or approval path?
- Marissa: from CS/partner ops standpoint, is roll-forward feasible without re-creating accounts or breaking our promo logic? We should avoid manual work per-company if possible.
- Ben: can you own commercial language and a short amendment to the incubator offer if we get sign-off?

If everyone’s OK, I propose a 50% roll-forward + 30-day extended onboarding credits as a middle ground (splits risk and keeps budget visible). I can draft the amendment and the HubSpot deal tag (DEAL-2027-3498).

Thanks —
Priyom
[Attachments: Nest_Incubator_SOW.pdf, usage_history_sept2027.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Incubator credits question: grandfathering from last cohort

Thanks for the background. I’m sympathetic to keeping partner workflows simple — Nest is strategic and repeatable. Operational notes:

- Promo system: we can automate a roll-forward if credits were issued as a named promo code per account. If credits are attached to a one-off coupon ID, we’ll need a short script to re-assign 50% to the new account IDs. That’s ~2-3 engineer-hours; partner ops can coordinate.
- Finance: Naomi — I’d prefer a tracked promo code (so it hits marketing/promotions expense) rather than a manual write-off. Keeps visibility and GAAP alignment.
- Suggested split: 50% roll-forward + 30-day onboarding top-up (not token-heavy) — this keeps the cohort teams productive and limits exposure.

If we go that route I recommend a one-page amendment: a table with original pilot credits, verified unused balance, roll-forward amount, and the 30-day onboarding credit schedule. Ben — I can help draft the amendment and the operational playbook.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Li <samantha@nestincubator.org>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts@nestincubator.org
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incubator credits question: grandfathering from last cohort

Hi Priyom — really appreciate the quick coordination and the practical compromise. Nest is happy to move forward with the 50% roll-forward + 30-day onboarding top-up approach.

Next steps from our side: I’ll upload the per-company usage CSV (as discussed) to the Google Drive link you provided and confirm the final list of 10 companies by Sep 30. We’d also like a short amendment and a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we can include in sponsor collateral — can you or Ben share that draft by Oct 4?

If that timeline works I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync for Oct 5 to walk the MAP and the operational steps.

Thanks again —
Sam
Director, Programs | Nest Incubator
[Forwarded attachment retained: Nest_Incubator_SOW.pdf]
